hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
hero.body:
The Senate passed legislation early Friday to provide $69.5 billion in funding for immigration enforcement operations through 2029. The vote was 52 to 47, ending weeks of delays caused by disputes over provisions unrelated to border security.

The bill funds President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement agencies, including the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and other federal operations. The legislation faced fierce opposition from several Republicans upset that it did not bar the Trump administration from creating an anti-weaponization settlement fund worth $1.776 billion intended to compensate political allies.

The settlement fund became a flashpoint during negotiations, with critics arguing it should not be included in border security legislation. The final version passed without restrictions on the fund, allowing the administration to proceed with payments to individuals it claims were targeted by previous government actions.

The budget reconciliation package now moves to the House for final passage before reaching President Trump's desk for signature. The legislation represents one of the largest single investments in immigration enforcement in recent years, providing funding certainty for border operations through the remainder of Trump's term and beyond.

The passage followed a late-night session marked by procedural battles and amendments. Supporters argued the funding was essential to carry out the administration's border security priorities, while opponents raised concerns about both the cost and the inclusion of the settlement provision.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling narrows protections for minority voting rights
cards.teaser: A major Supreme Court decision has left voting rights advocates with limited options for protecting racial-minority voters.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling that significantly restricts how racial-minority voting rights can be protected under federal law, marking a major shift in civil rights safeguards.

In response to the decision, advocates are focusing on state-level voting rights acts and redistricting strategies in Democratic-led states as the primary remaining tools for protecting minority voters' power.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes sweeping gun regulations rollback
cards.teaser: The administration is advancing the broadest firearm deregulation in years, dismantling rules on handgun shipping and background checks.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is undertaking a wide-ranging rollback of firearm regulations, proposing changes that would allow Americans to mail handguns, weaken Biden-era background check requirements, and make it more difficult to revoke gun dealer licenses. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is leading the effort, which includes dismantling a 1927 criminal statute and dozens of newer rules.

Critics say the changes would allow more guns to move through commerce with less federal oversight. The proposals include gutting President Biden's effort to close the gun show loophole, which required background checks for sales at gun shows and online. The administration's plan represents the most comprehensive deregulation of firearms in years.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit North Korea next week
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week for his first visit to the country since 2019, according to multiple news sources. The trip will feature meetings with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, representing a significant diplomatic engagement between the two nations during a period of considerable regional tension.

The visit occurs just weeks after Xi held separate meetings with the leaders of the United States and Russia, both countries that significantly influence North Korea's foreign policy decisions. The timing underscores China's effort to maintain its influence over its nuclear-armed neighbor as regional security dynamics continue to evolve.

China remains North Korea's most vital ally and primary trading partner. Beijing provides crucial economic support and diplomatic backing at the United Nations. For China, North Korea holds strategic value as a buffer state positioned between Chinese territory and U.S.-allied South Korea. Xi's previous visit to Pyongyang in 2019 occurred during a period when North Korea and the United States were engaged in diplomatic discussions, though those negotiations eventually faltered.

The announcement arrives at a moment when North Korea continues advancing its nuclear weapons program. China, meanwhile, manages increasingly complex relationships with Washington and Moscow while attempting to preserve stability on the Korean Peninsula. Beijing must balance its own interests against those of neighboring countries and major global powers.

The specific agenda for Xi's visit remains undisclosed, though discussions are expected to center on bilateral relations and regional security matters. The meeting between Xi and Kim will receive close attention from regional observers seeking to understand how China intends to navigate its relationship with North Korea within the current geopolitical landscape.

This diplomatic engagement highlights the enduring importance of the China-North Korea relationship despite years of strain and cooling ties. The two nations share a long history of strategic partnership, though their relationship has experienced periods of distance and tension, particularly following North Korea's nuclear weapons development.

The visit takes place as both countries face external pressures and shifting international dynamics. North Korea continues to pursue its weapons programs despite international sanctions, while China works to maintain its position as a regional power amid its own complicated relationships with the West. The meeting provides an opportunity for both leaders to reaffirm their alliance and coordinate positions on matters affecting the Korean Peninsula and broader regional security.

For South Korea and other regional stakeholders, the visit carries significant implications. How China exercises its influence over North Korea could affect prospects for dialogue, stability, and the trajectory of inter-Korean relations. The meeting may also signal Beijing's priorities regarding tensions on the peninsula and its approach to managing North Korea's nuclear capabilities within the context of broader U.S.-China competition.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy proposes direct talks with Putin
cards.teaser: Zelenskyy sent an open letter to Russian President Putin proposing face-to-face negotiations to end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sent an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin proposing face-to-face negotiations to end the war. Zelenskyy emphasized that only direct engagement between the two countries could resolve the conflict, particularly as US attention has shifted toward Iran.

The Kremlin confirmed that Putin has been briefed on Zelenskyy's letter. The proposal marks a diplomatic move as the war continues, with Zelenskyy calling for direct talks between the two leaders.

cards.headline: AI industry groups accuse China of fueling opposition to US data centers
cards.teaser: Pro-AI organizations say China-linked actors are using social media bots to stoke resistance to data center construction across the country.
cards.body:
AI industry advocates claim China-linked actors are using social media to amplify opposition to data centers that power artificial intelligence systems in the United States. Pro-AI groups say they have tracked what they believe are bot-driven messages designed to increase resistance to data center construction.

The resistance to data centers has emerged as a threat to the AI industry's expansion plans, with local communities raising concerns about energy costs and job impacts. Industry leaders argue that foreign actors are exploiting these concerns to slow American AI development.

cards.headline: Energy Department official leads Trump science and technology strategy
cards.teaser: Energy undersecretary Daro Gil is working to strengthen US competitiveness in science and technology while high-profile AI policy fights dominate headlines.
cards.body:
Energy Department undersecretary Daro Gil is quietly leading efforts to advance US science and technology competitiveness during President Trump's second term. While dramatic disputes over AI policy have captured public attention, Gil has focused on long-term strategic planning for American technological leadership.

Gil's approach contrasts with the reactive pattern that has dominated AI policymaking, where officials scramble to respond after AI labs release powerful new models. His work at the Energy Department emphasizes building sustained competitive advantages in science and technology rather than responding to immediate crises. The role has kept him largely out of the public eye while congressional and state efforts to regulate AI have generated controversy.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy proposes direct talks with Putin
cards.teaser: Zelenskyy sent an open letter to Russian President Putin proposing face-to-face negotiations to end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sent an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin proposing face-to-face negotiations to end the war. Zelenskyy emphasized that only direct engagement between the two countries could resolve the conflict, particularly as US attention has shifted toward Iran.

The Kremlin confirmed that Putin has been briefed on Zelenskyy's letter. The proposal marks a diplomatic move as the war continues, with Zelenskyy calling for direct talks between the two leaders.

cards.headline: Russia floods Armenia with disinformation ahead of election
cards.teaser: Groups linked to the Kremlin and Russian intelligence agencies have sought to discredit Armenia's prime minister.
cards.body:
Russia has launched a disinformation campaign targeting Armenia's upcoming election, with groups connected to the Kremlin and Russian intelligence agencies working to undermine Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. The effort signals Moscow's anxiety about its waning influence in the former Soviet republic.

Pashinyan is running for re-election as Armenia confronts critical decisions about its future, including questions of war and peace, democratic governance, and geopolitical alignment. The prime minister has gained support from former US President Trump, while facing opposition from Russian President Putin.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Pashinyan seeks re-election amid geopolitical tensions
cards.teaser: Nikol Pashinyan faces an election as Armenia weighs questions of war, peace, democracy, and independence.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is campaigning for re-election in a vote that will shape the country's future direction on fundamental issues. The election comes as Armenia faces decisions about war and peace, autocracy and democracy, and subjugation versus independence.

Pashinyan has received support from former US President Trump while facing opposition from Russian President Putin. The geopolitical divide reflects Armenia's position between competing powers as it seeks to chart its course forward.

cards.headline: Gold mining fuels Ebola spread in Congo
cards.teaser: Mining activity in a remote Congolese town is driving the spread of a devastating Ebola outbreak.
cards.body:
Gold mining operations in a remote hill town in Congo are contributing to the spread of an Ebola outbreak in the region. Mining has been the economic foundation of the area for decades, but the activity is now creating conditions that allow the deadly virus to spread more rapidly.

The outbreak represents a public health crisis in an area where mining brings workers and communities into closer contact. The connection between mining operations and disease transmission highlights the challenges of controlling Ebola in regions where economic activity depends on resource extraction.

cards.headline: Australia seizes over 100,000 illegal cockroaches in record bust
cards.teaser: Australian authorities confiscated more than 100,000 illegal insects worth $200,000 from a breeder.
cards.body:
Australian authorities conducted a record-breaking seizure of over 100,000 illegal cockroaches from a breeder in New South Wales. The confiscated insects are valued at approximately $200,000 and include giant hissing cockroaches among other species.

The bust represents the largest seizure of illegal insects in Australian history. Authorities targeted an individual described as a cockroach kingpin who had been breeding and potentially selling the insects in violation of biosecurity and wildlife regulations.

cards.headline: Ex-wife of Dubai ruler's nephew reported in custody
cards.teaser: Zeynab Javadli had not been in contact with friends since Tuesday, according to prosecutors.
cards.body:
Zeynab Javadli, the former wife of the nephew of Dubai's ruler, is in custody according to prosecutors. Javadli had not been in contact with any of her friends since Tuesday, prompting concern about her whereabouts.

Prosecutors confirmed Javadli's custody status following inquiries about her disappearance. The circumstances surrounding her detention and the charges she may face have not been disclosed.

hero.headline: Teachers say AI will transform education more than internet or computers
hero.body:
A majority of K-12 teachers believe artificial intelligence will have a greater impact on education than the internet or computers, according to a new poll from NPR and Ipsos. The survey reveals a growing divide between the technology's practical applications and concerns about its effect on student learning.

Many teachers reported using AI to reduce their workload and save time on administrative tasks. The technology is being adopted across classrooms as educators experiment with ways to streamline lesson planning, grading, and other time-consuming responsibilities that have long burdened the profession.

Despite this adoption, a majority of teachers expressed worry that AI is making it harder for students to develop independent thinking skills. The concern centers on whether students are using the technology as a shortcut that bypasses the critical thinking and problem-solving processes that traditional learning methods require.

The poll highlights tension between efficiency and educational outcomes as schools integrate AI tools. Teachers find themselves balancing the benefits of reduced administrative burden against potential risks to student development. The technology's rapid integration into classrooms has outpaced clear guidelines on best practices for its use.

The findings suggest AI represents a turning point in American education, with teachers recognizing both its transformative potential and the challenges it poses. As schools continue adopting these tools, educators are navigating uncharted territory in determining how to harness AI's capabilities while preserving the learning experiences that help students think independently.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling narrows protections for minority voting rights
cards.teaser: A major Supreme Court decision has left voting rights advocates with limited options for protecting racial-minority voters.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling that significantly restricts how racial-minority voting rights can be protected under federal law, marking a major shift in civil rights safeguards.

In response to the decision, advocates are focusing on state-level voting rights acts and redistricting strategies in Democratic-led states as the primary remaining tools for protecting minority voters' power.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy killed in stabbing, girlfriend's son arrested
cards.teaser: James Handy, known for roles in Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick, was stabbed to death at age 81.
cards.body:
Actor James Handy died after being stabbed. Police arrested the son of his girlfriend in connection with the killing. Handy was 81 years old at the time of his death.

Handy appeared in several major films during his career, including Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick. His work in Hollywood spanned multiple decades and included roles in widely recognized productions.

cards.headline: Senate approves $70 billion immigration enforcement funding bill
cards.teaser: The Senate passed legislation funding immigration enforcement agencies after weeks of delays over a settlement fund.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a $70 billion bill early Friday morning to fund President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement agencies. The legislation had stalled for weeks amid intense opposition to an unrelated $1.776 billion settlement fund included in the measure.

Lawmakers ultimately approved the bill without placing restrictions on the settlement fund, breaking the deadlock that had blocked its progress through the chamber.

cards.headline: Scientists develop AI-powered robots to automate laboratory research
cards.teaser: Researchers are building autonomous robotic labs that use artificial intelligence to conduct experiments.
cards.body:
Scientists are building autonomous robotic laboratories powered by artificial intelligence to handle scientific experiments with minimal human oversight. These AI-driven systems are designed to take over the most time-consuming and repetitive tasks that currently consume researchers' hours.

By automating these laborious aspects of laboratory work, researchers can redirect their efforts toward analysis and scientific discovery. This shift in how experiments are conducted could significantly change the landscape of research productivity.

cards.headline: World Cup sticker collecting gains popularity in United States
cards.teaser: Collecting Panini stickers for the World Cup, long popular in Europe and Latin America, is drawing more interest from American fans.
cards.body:
For many fans, the World Cup begins with a pack of stickers. Collecting Panini stickers is a tradition that has long been beloved in Europe and Latin America. Now the U.S. is catching up, with interest building steadily as the tournament approaches.

This summer, the buzz around sticker collecting in America is bigger than ever. The hobby involves purchasing packs of stickers featuring World Cup players and teams, then trading duplicates with other collectors to complete an album.

cards.headline: Royal family member Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was subletting Royal Lodge cottages
cards.teaser: A public spending watchdog found that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor sublet cottages on the Royal Lodge property.
cards.body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had been subletting cottages at Royal Lodge, according to a public spending watchdog. The examination looked into property arrangements involving members of the royal family.

The watchdog's findings reveal details about how Andrew used the property beyond his own residence. Royal Lodge has been his home, but the subletting arrangement adds another dimension to questions about royal property use and public funds.

hero.headline: S&P Declines to Fast-Track SpaceX Into Benchmark Index
hero.body:
S&P Global has reaffirmed its existing index inclusion rules and will not make exceptions for SpaceX, even as the company prepares for one of the largest initial public offerings in history. The decision means SpaceX will need to meet standard criteria before gaining entry to benchmark indexes like the S&P 500.

SpaceX is opening shares to individual investors starting next week, marking the transition of Elon Musk's company from private to public ownership. The company's significant scale had prompted speculation about whether S&P would modify its traditional eligibility requirements to accommodate such a major offering.

S&P's existing rules require companies to demonstrate positive earnings over multiple quarters and maintain sufficient public float before qualifying for benchmark index inclusion. These requirements serve an important function by ensuring that only financially stable companies with adequate liquidity become part of indexes that underpin trillions of dollars in passive investment funds. When a company enters an index, it triggers automatic purchases from funds tracking those benchmarks, creating substantial demand for shares.

The ruling establishes precedent for other large private companies considering public offerings. By maintaining consistent standards regardless of company size or market impact, S&P preserves the integrity of its methodology, which institutional investors depend on for portfolio construction and risk management.

SpaceX will enter public markets without the immediate advantage of index-driven buying that accompanies S&P 500 membership. The company will need to demonstrate sustained profitability and satisfy all standard requirements before index funds are compelled to purchase its shares. Depending on financial performance and how quickly SpaceX meets eligibility criteria, this timeline could span quarters or potentially years following the initial public offering.

The decision affects not just SpaceX but sets a broader precedent for mega-IPOs, according to reporting from Bloomberg and other outlets. S&P's approach underscores that the company will apply the same standards to all offerings, regardless of the company's prominence or anticipated market impact.

This outcome represents a reality check for SpaceX and highlights the distinction between a company's market significance and its readiness for passive index inclusion. While SpaceX's public debut will undoubtedly attract substantial investor interest and media attention, the company will need to build a track record of profitable operations before benefiting from the automatic purchasing power that comes with being a component of major benchmark indexes.

The indexing decision does not prevent SpaceX shares from being purchased by active investors or included in funds that use different methodologies. However, it does defer the automatic demand that would flow from the passive investing ecosystem that tracks major benchmarks.

cards.headline: SpaceX Opens Share Purchases to Individual Investors
cards.teaser: Individual investors will be able to buy stakes in Elon Musk's space and AI company starting next week.
cards.body:
SpaceX will begin allowing individual investors to purchase shares in the company starting next week, expanding ownership beyond institutional and accredited investors. The move represents a significant shift for Elon Musk's privately held company, which operates businesses ranging from rocket launches to artificial intelligence development.

The offering gives retail investors direct access to a company that has been among the most closely watched private firms in the technology sector. SpaceX has maintained private status longer than many comparable technology companies, limiting investment opportunities primarily to venture capital firms and wealthy individuals meeting accredited investor requirements.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls Near $62,000 as AI Trade Unwinds
cards.teaser: Bitcoin extended its longest losing streak since August as cryptocurrency markets faced a deepening selloff.
cards.body:
Bitcoin has dropped to near $62,000, its lowest level since February, as investors unwind positions in AI-related trades across cryptocurrency markets. The decline marks the digital currency's longest consecutive losing streak since August.

The selloff reflects a broader retreat from speculative technology investments that had previously driven cryptocurrency prices higher. Bitcoin's slide has erased earlier gains accumulated during periods of stronger market sentiment toward digital assets.

cards.headline: Nvidia Approves All Three Major Memory Makers for Next-Generation Chips
cards.teaser: Nvidia cleared Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron to supply HBM4 memory for its upcoming Vera Rubin processors.
cards.body:
Nvidia has qualified all three major memory chip manufacturers to supply HBM4 memory for its next-generation Vera Rubin processors, according to CEO Jensen Huang. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have all passed Nvidia's technical requirements for the advanced memory technology.

The approval gives Nvidia multiple suppliers for a critical component in its artificial intelligence processors. Huang stated the company will allocate memory supply carefully among the three qualified manufacturers. HBM4 represents the next generation of high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators and advanced computing applications.

cards.headline: Graduates Face Long-Term Wage Impact from Weak Job Market
cards.teaser: Recent college graduates entering a soft hiring environment may experience lasting effects on earnings and career opportunities.
cards.body:
College graduates entering the workforce during the current hiring downturn face potential long-term wage consequences. Research on previous economic cycles shows that workers who begin their careers during recessions or hiring slowdowns typically earn significantly less than peers who graduate during stronger economic periods, with wage gaps persisting for a decade or more.

The full impact of this hiring downturn on recent graduates will take years to fully understand. Artificial intelligence's role in reshaping employment patterns adds another layer of uncertainty to how this period will ultimately affect their career trajectories and earnings potential.

cards.headline: Anthropic Co-Founder Warns Against Autonomous AI Development
cards.teaser: Jack Clark said artificial intelligence could reach a point where it advances without human oversight.
cards.body:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark has called for safeguards to prevent artificial intelligence systems from developing autonomously without human involvement. Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Clark warned that AI technology could evolve to a stage where it progresses independently of human direction or input.

The statement comes from a leader at one of the prominent AI safety-focused companies competing in the artificial intelligence sector. Anthropic has positioned itself as prioritizing responsible AI development alongside building advanced language models and other AI systems.

cards.headline: Mattel Tests Entertainment Strategy with He-Man Franchise
cards.teaser: The toy maker is attempting to build an entertainment business around the 1980s Masters of the Universe character.
cards.body:
Mattel is betting on Masters of the Universe as it expands into entertainment production. The 2026 film, with a $200 million budget, represents a major test of whether the toy company can successfully adapt older intellectual property for modern audiences.

The project faces skepticism in a landscape where recent hits have centered on properties audiences actively care about or original ideas entirely. Few revival films from established franchises have succeeded in recent years, making Mattel's He-Man venture a risky gamble compared to its successful 2023 Barbie adaptation.

hero.headline: Valve confirms Steam Machine gaming console will ship this summer
hero.body:
Valve has announced that its Steam Machine gaming console will launch this summer, along with a Steam Frame VR headset. The company shared the news in a blog post detailing its Verified programs for both devices, ending months of uncertainty about when the long-delayed hardware would finally reach consumers.

The Steam Machine represents Valve's push to bring its gaming platform into living rooms through a dedicated console device. Rather than relying solely on PC gaming and its Steam Deck handheld, the company is now targeting the traditional home console market. This puts Valve in direct competition with established players like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo, though the company has a significant advantage: its massive library of games already available on the Steam platform.

The simultaneous launch of the Steam Machine and Steam Frame suggests Valve is planning a coordinated expansion of its hardware ecosystem. Both devices have been in development for some time, and this summer announcement finally provides players and developers with a concrete release window after years of waiting.

Valve has positioned itself as a major player in gaming hardware over the past several years. The Steam Deck established the company's credibility in the space by proving that Valve could design and manufacture handheld gaming devices successfully. The Steam Machine builds on that foundation by extending the company's reach into the living room, leveraging its distribution platform and existing game library as key competitive advantages.

The company has not yet disclosed detailed specifications, pricing information, or exact launch dates for either device. These details will likely emerge in the coming months as the summer window approaches. Developers using Steam's Verified program will have time to prepare their titles for the new hardware.

The gaming hardware market has become increasingly competitive in recent years. Traditional console makers continue to release new generations of devices while PC gaming experiences strong growth. Streaming services and cloud gaming have also changed how players think about accessing games. Valve's entry into the living room console space capitalizes on trends that have been favorable to the company, but the company will need to execute effectively on both hardware and software to succeed against entrenched competitors.

The summer launch will be a significant test for Valve. Success in the handheld market with the Steam Deck does not guarantee success in the home console space, where consumer expectations and competitive pressures are different. However, Valve's control over Steam, its massive catalog of games, and its established relationship with PC gamers give it unique advantages as it attempts to translate its digital distribution dominance into the living room gaming market.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI chief criticizes Anthropic models as too expensive
cards.teaser: Microsoft's AI chief said Anthropic's AI models carry pricing that makes them impractical for widespread deployment.
cards.body:
Microsoft's head of artificial intelligence stated that Anthropic's AI models are priced at levels that limit their practical use. The comments came during Microsoft's Build 2026 developer conference.

The pricing dispute reflects broader questions about the economics of AI development and deployment as companies race to build and scale these technologies. Microsoft has invested heavily in OpenAI and developed its own AI model family, while Anthropic has emerged as a well-funded competitor. Anthropic's annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up dramatically from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025, ahead of the company's anticipated IPO.

cards.headline: Anthropic reports revenue crossed $47 billion annually ahead of planned IPO
cards.teaser: Anthropic announced annualized revenue reached $47 billion in May as the company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced that its annualized revenue reached $47 billion in May, a dramatic increase from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company disclosed these figures as it prepares for an initial public offering.

Co-founder Daniela Amodei addressed investor concerns about returns on AI investments amid the company's rapid expansion. Anthropic continues to compete with OpenAI and other major players in the increasingly crowded artificial intelligence sector.

cards.headline: Researchers identify 80-meter tree as tallest in East Asia after years of searching
cards.teaser: A Taiwania cryptomerioides tree nicknamed 'The Heaven Sword' has been crowned East Asia's tallest tree following a nearly decade-long search.
cards.body:
Scientists identified an 80-meter Taiwania cryptomerioides tree as the tallest in East Asia after years of systematic searching. The tree, nicknamed 'The Heaven Sword,' represents the culmination of a research effort that spanned nearly a decade.

The discovery required extensive fieldwork and measurement techniques to confirm the tree's record-breaking height. Taiwania cryptomerioides is a conifer species native to parts of East Asia. The identification of this particular specimen provides researchers with valuable data about old-growth forests and tree growth patterns in the region.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic storm may bring northern lights to parts of United States
cards.teaser: A geomagnetic storm could make the aurora borealis visible across northern states including Utah, North Carolina, Vermont, Illinois, and Oregon.
cards.body:
Space weather forecasters issued a G3 geomagnetic storm watch for June 4-5, with four Earth-directed coronal mass ejections potentially triggering aurora displays. The storm could make the northern lights visible as far south as Illinois and Oregon.

States including Utah, North Carolina, Vermont, and New Hampshire received aurora forecasts for the event. Geomagnetic storms occur when solar material interacts with Earth's magnetic field, creating the colorful light displays typically seen only at high latitudes. The G3 classification indicates a strong storm capable of pushing the aurora viewing zone southward from its typical Arctic locations.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky plans to launch new AI laboratory
cards.teaser: Brian Chesky announced plans to establish an artificial intelligence lab, explaining previous hesitation about AI partnerships.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to establish a new AI laboratory. The move represents the company's decision to develop artificial intelligence capabilities internally rather than partnering with existing large language model providers.

Chesky had previously explained that Airbnb declined to pursue LLM partnerships because current products weren't sufficiently developed for the company's needs. The dedicated lab will enable Airbnb to build AI tools tailored specifically for travel and hospitality applications.

cards.headline: Mangrove forests show recovery after decades of human destruction
cards.teaser: Mangrove forests are staging a comeback globally after years of human-caused damage, benefiting coastal communities and climate.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests are making an unexpected comeback in multiple locations after being severely damaged by human activity. These swampy coastal ecosystems are staging a surprise recovery that brings benefits to both climate and communities.

The return of mangroves matters significantly for coastal protection and carbon storage. These forests act as natural barriers against storms and flooding while sequestering carbon from the atmosphere. They also provide critical habitat for marine species and help stabilize shorelines in tropical and subtropical regions around the world.

hero.headline: Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge diagnosed with rib stress fracture
hero.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has been diagnosed with a rib stress fracture and will be reevaluated in four to six weeks. The diagnosis was announced after Judge missed his third consecutive game. The injury sidelines one of baseball's most prominent players during a critical stretch of the season.

Judge, who has been a cornerstone of the Yankees lineup, now faces an extended absence as the team awaits further clarity on his recovery timeline. The Yankees are in a holding pattern as medical staff monitor his progress. The injury occurred during recent play, though the specific incident that caused the stress fracture has not been detailed in team announcements.

The rib stress fracture represents a significant blow to the Yankees' offensive capabilities. Judge's absence will require the team to adjust its batting order and outfield configuration. The four to six week reevaluation window means Judge will miss multiple series, putting pressure on other roster members to fill the production gap.

Stress fractures in the ribs are particularly challenging for baseball players because the throwing and swinging motions required in the sport engage the core and ribcage extensively. Recovery requires complete rest from baseball activities to allow the bone to heal properly. Rushing back too quickly can result in complications or a more severe fracture.

The Yankees have not announced roster moves to replace Judge on the active lineup, but will need to rely on bench depth and potentially call up minor league players to cover his position. The team's performance over the next month will largely depend on how well the remaining roster compensates for the loss of one of their top offensive threats. Judge's status will be reassessed after the initial recovery period to determine when he can resume baseball activities.

cards.headline: Carolina Hurricanes defeat Vegas Golden Knights in overtime in Stanley Cup Final Game 2
cards.teaser: Seth Jarvis scored in overtime to give the Hurricanes a Game 2 victory over the Golden Knights in the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Seth Jarvis scored on a power play 3:56 into overtime to give the Carolina Hurricanes a 4-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final. The win came after the Hurricanes mounted a dramatic third-period comeback, erasing a two-goal deficit before Vegas tied the game late in regulation.

The third period was thrilling, featuring four goals and another that was disallowed due to goaltender interference. A failed Vegas challenge set up the crucial power play that led to Jarvis's winning goal. The series is now tied at one game each as play shifts back to Vegas.

cards.headline: Andy Farrell signs new Ireland rugby contract through 2031
cards.teaser: Ireland men's rugby head coach Andy Farrell has agreed to a new deal with the Irish Rugby Football Union that extends his tenure through 2031.
cards.body:
Ireland men's head coach Andy Farrell has signed a new contract with the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) that will keep him in the role until 2031.

The contract extension represents a significant commitment to the long-term direction of the Ireland men's rugby program as it continues competing at international level.

cards.headline: Arsenal trio and Bruno Fernandes nominated for PFA men's player of the year
cards.teaser: Six players including three from Arsenal have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers' Association men's player of the year award.
cards.body:
Arsenal's Declan Rice, Gabriel, and David Raya have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers' Association men's player of the year award alongside Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, and Rayan Cherki.

The six-player shortlist represents the top performers in English football this season. Professional players cast the votes to determine the winner of the prestigious annual award.

cards.headline: Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa shortlisted for PFA women's player of the year
cards.teaser: Two Manchester City players are among the nominees for the Professional Footballers' Association Women's Player of the Year award.
cards.body:
Manchester City duo Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers' Association's Women's Player of the Year award. Shaw, known by her nickname 'Bunny', and midfielder Hasegawa are among those in contention for the top individual honour in women's football.

The award is determined by votes from professional players across the women's game in England.

cards.headline: FIFA demands payment from fans mistakenly given free World Cup tickets
cards.teaser: World Cup organizers are requiring fans who received tickets in error without payment to pay within seven days or forfeit their seats.
cards.body:
FIFA has acknowledged a ticketing error that gave some fans complimentary tickets to World Cup group stage matches in Toronto. The organization now requires those supporters to pay for the seats within seven days or forfeit access to the games.

FIFA expressed regret over the mistake but is firm in its payment demand. Fans who received the erroneous free tickets must complete their purchases during the specified window to keep their seats for the group stage matches.

cards.headline: NBA commissioner warns of severe consequences after court invasion
cards.teaser: Adam Silver said major sporting events provide a platform for inappropriate behavior and cautioned fans that punishments for court invasions are serious.
cards.body: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has cautioned fans against disrupting games, describing court invasions as "stupid" and warning that penalties will be severe. Silver noted that major sporting events provide a high-profile platform that some individuals exploit inappropriately. The commissioner's comments emphasize the league's zero-tolerance approach to security breaches during games.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy stabbed to death in Los Angeles
hero.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old veteran character actor, was fatally stabbed at his home in Tarzana, California. Police discovered him in the front yard with multiple stab wounds to the chest at around 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. He was unconscious when officers arrived at the scene.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested and charged on suspicion of murder. Bail was set at $2 million. According to the Los Angeles Police Department, Gledhill called 911 and told the dispatcher, "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for."

The police statement noted that Gledhill resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend. No other suspects are being sought in connection with the killing.

Handy built a lengthy career in film and television spanning multiple decades. Born in New York City, he began his acting work in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. Over his career, he appeared in numerous productions across both mediums, often taking on character roles and supporting parts in ensemble casts.

His filmography includes appearances in the 1995 adventure film Jumanji and the 2022 action sequel Top Gun: Maverick, which introduced him to audiences of a new generation. He also appeared in Logan and K-911. His television credits include roles in Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His most recent film work was Top Gun: Maverick in 2022.

The Los Angeles Police Department is continuing to investigate the incident. The case will be presented to prosecutors for potential charges against Gledhill.

Handy's death marks a violent conclusion to a career that stretched across multiple generations of filmmaking. As a veteran character actor, he had established himself as a reliable presence in supporting roles throughout Hollywood productions. His work in recent major films had demonstrated his continued relevance in the industry even as he entered his ninth decade.

The incident has drawn significant media attention given Handy's appearances in well-known films and television programs. His contributions to entertainment spanned from the late 1970s through 2022, providing a substantial body of work across numerous genres and production types.

cards.headline: Mobo Awards founder Kanya King dies at 57
cards.teaser: King, who mortgaged her house to launch the music awards ceremony 30 years ago, had been treated for cancer.
cards.body:
Kanya King, the founder of the Mobo Awards, has died at age 57. King had been receiving treatment for cancer before her death.

King established the Mobo Awards three decades ago after mortgaging her home to fund the launch of the ceremony. The awards celebrate music of black origin and have become a prominent fixture in the British music industry, recognizing artists across genres including hip-hop, R&B, gospel, and jazz.

cards.headline: Scary Movie reboot earns $7.5 million in Thursday previews
cards.teaser: The horror comedy franchise's latest installment opened with preview numbers approaching those of Scream 7.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie film earned $7.5 million in Thursday night preview screenings, matching the performance of the recent Scream 7 release. Masters of the Universe collected $4 million in its Thursday previews.

The sixth installment of the parody franchise marks the series' return after more than a decade. The film takes aim at multiple horror properties, though reviewers found that successful jokes are sparse throughout the movie.

cards.headline: Steve Lacy announces new album with single release
cards.teaser: The musician released "The Feeling," the first track from his third album Oh Yeah?, set to arrive in July.
cards.body:
Steve Lacy is releasing a new album called Oh Yeah? in July. He has shared the single "The Feeling" to announce the project, which marks his third studio album.

Lacy has established himself as a versatile artist working across solo releases and production work, with a focus on alternative R&B.

cards.headline: China increases regulation of viral micro dramas
cards.teaser: Authorities are targeting content featuring sexual themes, violence, and materialism in short-form video dramas that have surged in popularity.
cards.body:
Chinese regulators are cracking down on micro dramas that contain what officials describe as soft pornography, violence, and materialistic content. The short-form video series have become increasingly popular on Chinese platforms.

The dramas have drawn criticism for sensationalist content despite their growing viewership. Authorities have not detailed specific enforcement measures but indicated they will increase oversight of the format as it continues to attract audiences across social media platforms.

cards.headline: Tinashe releases new single "Too Easy"
cards.teaser: The singer previewed the track during her DJ set at Coachella earlier this year.
cards.body:
Tinashe has released a new single called "Too Easy." The singer first played the song during a DJ set at the Coachella music festival months earlier.

The release continues Tinashe's independent music career following her departure from major label RCA Records. She has maintained a steady output of music and performances while building a dedicated fan base outside the traditional label system.

cards.headline: Shaboozey releases "Cowgirl" music video featuring reality TV star
cards.teaser: The musician cast Summer House star Ciara Miller in the video for a track from his upcoming album.
cards.body:
Shaboozey has released a music video for his song "Cowgirl" featuring Ciara Miller from the reality series Summer House. The track will appear on his forthcoming album The Outlaw Cherie Lee Other Western Tales.

The collaboration brings together the musician's country-influenced sound with a figure from reality television. Shaboozey has been building momentum in the music industry with his distinctive blend of country and hip-hop influences.

hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
hero.body:
The Senate passed legislation early Friday to provide $69.5 billion in funding for immigration enforcement operations through 2029. The vote was 52 to 47, ending weeks of delays caused by disputes over provisions unrelated to border security.

The bill funds President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement agencies, including the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and other federal operations. The legislation faced fierce opposition from several Republicans upset that it did not bar the Trump administration from creating an anti-weaponization settlement fund worth $1.776 billion intended to compensate political allies.

The settlement fund became a flashpoint during negotiations, with critics arguing it should not be included in border security legislation. The final version passed without restrictions on the fund, allowing the administration to proceed with payments to individuals it claims were targeted by previous government actions.

The budget reconciliation package now moves to the House for final passage before reaching President Trump's desk for signature. The legislation represents one of the largest single investments in immigration enforcement in recent years, providing funding certainty for border operations through the remainder of Trump's term and beyond.

The passage followed a late-night session marked by procedural battles and amendments. Supporters argued the funding was essential to carry out the administration's border security priorities, while opponents raised concerns about both the cost and the inclusion of the settlement provision.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes sweeping gun regulations rollback
cards.teaser: The administration is advancing the broadest firearm deregulation in years, dismantling rules on handgun shipping and background checks.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is undertaking a wide-ranging rollback of firearm regulations, proposing changes that would allow Americans to mail handguns, weaken Biden-era background check requirements, and make it more difficult to revoke gun dealer licenses. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is leading the effort, which includes dismantling a 1927 criminal statute and dozens of newer rules.

Critics say the changes would allow more guns to move through commerce with less federal oversight. The proposals include gutting President Biden's effort to close the gun show loophole, which required background checks for sales at gun shows and online. The administration's plan represents the most comprehensive deregulation of firearms in years.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling leaves few options for protecting minority voting rights
cards.teaser: After a major Supreme Court decision, advocates are turning to state-level laws and redistricting strategies to preserve voting power for racial minorities.
cards.body:
A major Supreme Court decision has significantly restricted the federal tools available to protect racial minority voting rights. Civil rights advocates are now focusing on state-level strategies as primary alternatives.

State voting rights acts and redistricting efforts in Democratic-led states represent among the few remaining avenues for preserving voting power for minority communities. However, these state-level protections vary considerably and lack the uniform reach that federal law previously provided.

cards.headline: AI industry groups accuse China of fueling opposition to US data centers
cards.teaser: Pro-AI organizations say China-linked actors are using social media bots to stoke resistance to data center construction across the country.
cards.body:
AI industry advocates claim China-linked actors are using social media to amplify opposition to data centers that power artificial intelligence systems in the United States. Pro-AI groups say they have tracked what they believe are bot-driven messages designed to increase resistance to data center construction.

The resistance to data centers has emerged as a threat to the AI industry's expansion plans, with local communities raising concerns about energy costs and job impacts. Industry leaders argue that foreign actors are exploiting these concerns to slow American AI development.

cards.headline: Energy Department official leads Trump science and technology strategy
cards.teaser: Energy undersecretary Daro Gil is working to strengthen US competitiveness in science and technology while high-profile AI policy fights dominate headlines.
cards.body:
Energy Department undersecretary Daro Gil is quietly leading efforts to advance US science and technology competitiveness during President Trump's second term. While dramatic disputes over AI policy have captured public attention, Gil has focused on long-term strategic planning for American technological leadership.

Gil's approach contrasts with the reactive pattern that has dominated AI policymaking, where officials scramble to respond after AI labs release powerful new models. His work at the Energy Department emphasizes building sustained competitive advantages in science and technology rather than responding to immediate crises. The role has kept him largely out of the public eye while congressional and state efforts to regulate AI have generated controversy.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden cabinet member could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. If elected in November, she would become the first female Native American to serve as a state governor.

Haaland previously represented New Mexico in the US House of Representatives before serving in President Biden's cabinet as Interior Secretary.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra face Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Early results from California's gubernatorial primary show Steve Hilton leading among Republicans and Xavier Becerra ahead in the Democratic field. The race features three prominent Democrats: Representative Katie Porter, former hedge fund manager Tom Steyer, and former Health and Human Services Secretary Becerra. Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are competing for their party's nomination.

The winner will seek to replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who is term-limited and cannot run for reelection. California's primary system will narrow the field before the general election determines the next governor of the nation's most populous state.
